title: KV260 SmartConnect co-simulation — HANG REPRODUCED, root cause is sampler's non-AXI-Lite-compliant state machine
context: The DCP netlist inspection (results/kv260_dcp_netlist_inspection.json, commit e11a73a0) eliminated five hypotheses, leaving SmartConnect protocol interaction as the surviving candidate. This co-simulation puts SmartConnect (gate-level sim netlist from the project's IP cache) in the loop between an AXI-full master BFM and our sampler, exercising the same write+read scenarios from the bare-DUT testbench. Result: deterministic hang, same shape as on-hardware.

test_results.description: AXI-full write to CONTROL=0 via SmartConnect

progress.event: S00_AWREADY asserted after 32 cycles — SmartConnect accepted the address
S00_WREADY TIMEOUT (200 cycles, never asserted) — SmartConnect never accepted write data

test_results.description: AXI-full read of SPIN_COUNT via SmartConnect (expect 128)

progress.event: S00_ARREADY asserted after 0 cycles — SmartConnect accepted the address
S00_RVALID TIMEOUT — no read data ever returned

root_cause_analysis.offending_code: if (!axi_awready && S_AXI_AWVALID && S_AXI_WVALID) begin axi_awready <= 1'b1; ... end
root_cause_analysis.symmetric_code_at_line_339: if (!axi_wready && S_AXI_WVALID && S_AXI_AWVALID) begin axi_wready <= 1'b1; ... end
root_cause_analysis.explanation: Both AWREADY and WREADY in the sampler's state machine require BOTH valids (AWVALID AND WVALID) to coincide in the same clock cycle before either asserts. This is a common sin in hand-rolled AXI-Lite slaves (the Xilinx AXI-Lite template even has this pattern) but it is NOT AXI-Lite-spec-compliant. AXI-Lite §A3.3.1 explicitly states AW and W channels are independent and can be driven on different cycles.
root_cause_analysis.why_bare_dut_sim_passed: The bare-DUT testbench's master BFM drove both VALIDs high simultaneously and HELD them until ACK. Even with channel-skew scenarios, both VALIDs remained asserted so they eventually coincided. The coincidence requirement was tolerated — NOT because the RTL was correct, but because the BFM's behavior happened to avoid triggering the bug.
root_cause_analysis.why_smartconnect_exposes_it: SmartConnect has internal AW and W pipelines that are independent. On M00_AXI, it drives M00_AWVALID based on the AW pipeline state and M00_WVALID based on the W pipeline state. These state machines complete at different cycles. M00_AWVALID may be asserted for one cycle (SmartConnect considers it ACKd internally once AWREADY returns... but AWREADY never returns because the sampler is waiting for WVALID). M00_WVALID may subsequently rise alone. The sampler's state machine, requiring coincidence, never ACKs either. Classic AXI-Lite slave bug that only shows up behind a real AXI interconnect.

fix_proposal.approach: Rewrite the AW and W ACK logic to handle each channel independently. Add aw_done/w_done flags; BVALID asserts when both are set. Reset both flags on BREADY.
fix_proposal.validation_path: Re-run smartconnect_sampler_tb.sv after fix — expect all scenarios to pass. Then rebuild bitstream, redeploy, retry on-hardware.

hypotheses_state.hypothesis: RTL AXI-Lite protocol deadlock on split AW/W channels
hypotheses_state.note: The earlier xsim rejection was misleading — the BFM held both VALIDs, accidentally avoiding the bug. SmartConnect's behavior exposes it.

hypotheses_state.status: CONFIRMED BUT ON OUR SIDE — SmartConnect is doing the right thing; sampler's state machine is non-compliant
MOOT — not needed to explain the hang

retro_074_next_step: Apply the RTL fix, re-run smartconnect_sampler_tb.sv to verify in sim, then rebuild bitstream (~50 min), repackage app bundle, redeploy, attempt on-hardware AXI access. Total wallclock to closure: ~90 min.
